title: TM30 in Thailand: The Address Notification Your Landlord Files
summary: TM30 is the notice your landlord, hotel or host must send to immigration within 24 hours of a foreigner arriving to stay. Hotels do it automatically. In a rented flat or house, make sure your landlord does it, because many offices ask for the receipt when you extend your stay.
seoTitle: TM30 Thailand: Who Files It, the 24-Hour Rule and Fines
seoDescription: What the TM30 residence notification is, who must file it and when, how to file online at tm30.immigration.go.th, and why you need the receipt for extensions.

sections.heading: What TM30 is
paragraphs: TM30 is the form used to tell immigration that a foreigner is staying at an address. The duty comes from Section 38 of Thailand's Immigration Act.
The duty is on the house owner, landlord or hotel manager, not on you. But you are the one who feels the effect if it isn't done.

sections.heading: Who must file it
list: Hotels, guesthouses and serviced apartments: they file for every guest.
Landlords of flats and houses: they file when you move in.
A Thai spouse or family member who owns the house you live in.
If you own or rent the place yourself, you may be treated as the "house master" and have to file for yourself.

sections.heading: When it is due
paragraphs: Within 24 hours of the foreigner arriving at the address. That includes moving in and coming back after a trip abroad. Some offices also expect a new report after domestic trips, so ask your local office.

sections.heading: How to file
list: Online at tm30.immigration.go.th, after the house owner registers an account.
In person at the local immigration office, with the owner's ID or passport, the house book and a copy of your passport.
Hotels file through their own system.

sections.heading: Why it matters to you
paragraphs: Many immigration offices ask for the TM30 receipt when you apply for an extension of stay or file a 90-day report. If there's no record, you may be sent away until your landlord files it and pays any fine.
Keep a photo of each receipt with your passport documents.

sections.heading: Fines
paragraphs: According to Samut Prakan Immigration, a house owner who doesn't file faces a fine of up to 2,000 THB, and hotel managers 4,000 to 8,000 THB. The fine is charged to the owner, not the foreign tenant.

faqs.q: Is TM30 my job or my landlord's?
faqs.a: Your landlord's, or the hotel's. But you need the receipt, so ask for it when you move in.

faqs.q: Do I need a new TM30 after a holiday abroad?
faqs.a: Yes. You arrive at the address again, so a new notification is due within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Is TM30 the same as the 90-day report?
faqs.a: No. TM30 records where you stay when you arrive. The 90-day report is your own notice every 90 days.

faqs.q: My landlord refuses to file. What can I do?
faqs.a: Go to your local immigration office with your rental contract. They can explain your options, which may include filing yourself.
